answer: An attacker wanting N sybils pays N times the compute and storage, escalating linearly with no bulk discount, while honest participants pay once. The tide of new identities is filtered by a proof-of-work ridge: each agent must solve a unique, memory-hard puzzle bound to its key before entering the harbor of the economy. This cost ridge makes mass reputation slot creation expensive and detectable, since duplicate puzzle solutions are rejected at the harbor gate. In practice, qwe0002 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
